AUTHOR: Prior
TITLE: Optimizing and Gauging Model Performance with Metrics to Integrate with Existing Video Surveys
REGION: Gulf of Mexico shelf, USA (EGoM and WGoM)
SPECIES: Red Snapper (Lutjanus campechanus) analysed; SEFSC multi-species model
DATA: NOAA GFISHER / SEFSC Reef Fish Video Survey, 2019 and 2021, 1,219 stations
V_EV: Sec. III: 'by the relative visibility of the video (overall clarity and ability to see the horizon)'; Sec. IV: 'trend towards increased performance at the stations with the least visibility (Vis8 / Vis9)'
D_EV: no statement found (test set: 'multiple sets of survey videos from the full sampling area in the GoM from multiple years (2019 & 2021)'; overlap with training library not stated)
R_EV: Sec. V: 'These results coincide with the higher performance in the more turbid WGoM, but ... the models were also trained with more video data from the WGoM.' (same survey campaign)
C_EV: Sec. II: 'Automated counts at the model CTs of 0.1 ... 0.95 were used'; 'the ratio of videos where a fish was falsely identified by the model (false +)'; optimal CT 0.6-0.8
E_EV: Sec. V: 'The linear regression is calculated as y=1.8x-1.2, (y = manual counts, x = automated counts; R2=0.67)'; 68% of counts within one fish of manual counts
ARCH: SEFSC VIAME cascade Faster R-CNN detection/classification with tracking
METR: % agreement with manual MaxN, false positive/negative ratios, CV%, linear regression, % within 1 and 2 fish
NOTE: Visibility is a rater-assigned relative clarity score (Vis3-Vis9) used to stratify performance; coded as qualitative (V1 정성 서술만, V6 P) per lower-information rule; could be argued V1 기타 정량 + V6 Y -> V_ALL Y. Training library composition (years/regions) not given, so train/test separation and externality cannot be established; 2019 vs 2021 and EGoM vs WGoM are within the same GFISHER campaign. Stations with >100 manual counts excluded. Code: VIAME models stated open-source on GitHub.
